title: Touchscreen design guidelines for children under 9
statement:
For touchscreen designs aimed at children under 9, use big targets (NN/g recommends at least 2 cm × 2 cm for young children, four times the 1 cm × 1 cm adult guideline), rely on tapping and swiping, offer more than one way to complete an action (for example tap or drag), and avoid precision dragging or scrolling with a mouse or trackpad, which children in this age group found hard.

Options:
- 2 cm minimum targets: Primary tap targets of at least 2 cm × 2 cm (≈ 76 × 76 CSS px) for children under 9 (fits: playful, friendly, bold)
- Tap-or-drag flexibility: Dual-input actions: every drag interaction also works by tapping the destination or a large arrow button (fits: inclusive, forgiving, playful)
- Single big button: One large single-button primary action per screen (for example a single big Play button) (fits: simple, calm, gentle)
- Click-only desktop: Desktop: click-only or simple keyboard-arrow interactions for under-9s; no long-distance dragging, scroll-dependent tasks or small-target clicking (fits: simple, accessible, friendly)
- Recommend, don't navigate: Reduce navigation by recommending related content after each item instead of sending children back to a homepage (fits: curious, engaging, playful)
appliesWhen: Applies to: kids apps, kids websites, mobile web, educational games. Audience: children under 10.

source.title: Design for Kids Based on Their Stage of Physical Development
